questions.answer: Under the established CSS framework, candidates generally need a bachelor’s degree of at least second division/Grade C and must meet the prescribed age window, nationality/domicile and other conditions. questions.title: How should a candidate prepare current affairs?
questions.answer: Maintain a dated issue file. For each issue, record the background, latest verified facts, stakeholders, Pakistan’s interests, international-law or institutional context, competing explanations, policy options and sources. Revise primary data from government and multilateral sources; use newspapers for reporting and debate.

questions.title: What was the Lahore Resolution?
questions.answer: A resolution adopted by the All-India Muslim League at its Lahore session on 23 March 1940, calling for independent states in Muslim-majority zones of the north-western and eastern parts of British India. It became a central milestone in the Pakistan Movement.

questions.title: What is the difference between a primary source and a secondary source?
questions.answer: A primary source is a direct record such as a law, official dataset, speech, treaty or original report. A secondary source interprets or reports on primary materials. Good research uses both and checks claims against the closest reliable source.

questions.title: What is the 7th NFC Award distribution formula and provincial weighting?
questions.quick_answer: The 7th NFC Award distributes the provincial divisible pool using a multi-criteria formula: Population (82.0%), Poverty/Backwardness (10.3%), Revenue Collection (5.0%), and Inverse Population Density (2.7%).
questions.answer: Enacted in 2010 under Article 160(3A), the 7th NFC Award moved away from solely population-based allocation to a four-metric formula: Population gets 82.0% weight, Poverty/Backwardness 10.3%, Revenue Collection/Generation 5.0%, and Inverse Population Density 2.7%. The resulting provincial shares of the divisible pool are: Punjab 51.74%, Sindh 24.55%, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 14.62% (pre-merger), and Balochistan 9.09%.

questions.title: What is Pakistan’s national literacy rate according to HIES 2024–25?
questions.quick_answer: According to PBS HIES 2024–25, the national literacy rate for the population aged 10 and above is 63% (73% for males and 54% for females).
questions.answer: The PBS HIES 2024–25 Social Indicators Report records national literacy (aged 10+) at 63%. Male literacy stands at 73% compared to 54% for females. Urban literacy is 74% versus 55% in rural areas. Provincial breakdown: Punjab 68%, Sindh 58%, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 58%, and Balochistan 49%. In CSS essays, always specify whether citing HIES 10+ age criteria or Census 2023 age-15+ criteria.

questions.title: How much does Pakistan spend on public education as a share of GDP?
questions.quick_answer: Pakistan spent PKR 962 Billion on public education in FY25 (combined federal and provincial), amounting to approximately 0.8% of GDP.
questions.answer: According to Chapter 10 of the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025–26, total public education expenditure across federal and all provincial governments reached PKR 962 billion in FY25, representing roughly 0.8% of GDP.
